summaries: A U.S. Census Bureau and HUD statistical release on New Residential Construction (August 2022 data, released September 20, 2022). Relevant to the task: Table 1b provides "Not seasonally adjusted" monthly building permits in thousands of units, including "1 unit" (single-family) figures for the United States and the West region. For August 2022, it lists a U.S. national total of 80.9 thousand (exceeding the 80,000 threshold) and a corresponding West region count of 17.8 thousand. The document covers data up to August 2022, providing only this single data point for the required 2022/08–2025/05 timeframe. The values are marked preliminary ("p"), indicating they may be superseded by later releases per the task's precedence rule.

A U.S. Census Bureau and HUD press release on Monthly New Residential Construction for September 2022 (released October 19, 2022). Relevant to the task: Table 1b provides not seasonally adjusted building permits in thousands of units, including United States and West region "1 unit" (single-family) counts for 2021 through September 2022. For the task's filtering condition (national permits > 80,000), August 2022 qualifies with a U.S. total of 81.0 thousand and a West permit value of 17.7 thousand; September 2022 (70.9 thousand) does not. The document covers the start of the requested 2022/08–2025/05 period but ends at September 2022. August 2022 figures are marked revised, subject to updates in subsequent releases.

A U.S. Census Bureau and HUD statistical release on New Residential Construction for October 2022 (released November 17, 2022). Relevant to the task: Table 1b provides "Not seasonally adjusted" building permit data in thousands of units for January through October 2022. Within the task's specified start date of August 2022, this document shows that August 2022 is the only month where the U.S. national single-family permit total (81.0 thousand) exceeded 80,000, with a corresponding West region single-family permit count of 17.7 thousand. September and October 2022 national totals fell below the threshold. This document supplies one qualifying data point for the average calculation but does not contain data for the remainder of the required timeframe (November 2022 through May 2025).

A U.S. Census Bureau and HUD monthly statistical release on New Residential Construction for November 2022 (released December 20, 2022). Relevant to the task: Table 1b provides Not Seasonally Adjusted building permit data in thousands of units for the United States and the West region, covering monthly figures from January 2022 through November 2022. For the task's specified window (August 2022 to May 2025), this document covers August through November 2022. It lists national single-family (1 unit) totals to evaluate the > 80,000 threshold. Within this coverage, only August 2022 qualifies (81.0 thousand), with a corresponding West region single-family permit value of 17.7 thousand. September through November 2022 values are below the threshold. This document contributes data for the early portion of the required timeframe but does not extend to May 2025, and data may be subject to revision in later releases given the methodology change noted for 2023.

A U.S. Census Bureau and HUD press release (Release Number CB23-10, January 19, 2023) reporting monthly New Residential Construction statistics for December 2022. Relevant to the task: Table 1b provides not seasonally adjusted building permit data for privately-owned housing units, specifically single-family ("1 unit") authorizations in thousands of units for the United States and the West region. Within the task's specified period (August 2022 to May 2025), this document covers August through December 2022. It identifies August 2022 as the only month in this range where the national single-family permit total exceeded the 80,000 threshold (81.0 thousand), with a corresponding West region permit value of 17.7 thousand; September through December 2022 fall below the threshold. The December 2022 data is marked preliminary, and values for earlier months in this report may be superseded by subsequent releases in the collection per the task's precedence rule.
